key_insight: At test time, investing compute into verification (sampling + scoring/reranking) reduces instruction–action misalignment more effectively than further scaling the policy model or its training data. A dedicated verifier and more verification compute follow a favorable scaling law for embodied instruction following.
problem_solved: Bridges the "intention–action gap" in Vision–Language–Action models by reducing incorrect or misaligned actions produced in response to natural language instructions without retraining or heavily scaling the policy.
method: Characterize test-time scaling laws for embodied instruction following and show verifier compute/size yields larger marginal gains than policy scaling.
Generate multiple candidate action trajectories from a policy, then use a learned verifier to score alignment between each trajectory, the visual observations, and the instruction.
Select or rerank actions at inference based on verifier scores (sampling + reranking / search), allowing better alignment with fixed policies.
impact: Enables practitioners to improve robot instruction-following accuracy by allocating inference-time compute to verification rather than costly policy retraining or scaling. This provides a practical, modular path to safer and more reliable VLA systems.
visual_elements: Two-line plot comparing scaling curves: verifier compute vs. policy size showing steeper gains for verification
Pipeline diagram: policy generates candidate trajectories → verifier scores each → best action selected (sample-and-rerank)
Bar chart or heatmap of alignment error before/after verification across benchmarks/environments
Icon set illustrating components: language instruction, visual input, policy, verifier, final action
paper_title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment
paper_authors: Jacky Kwok, Xilun Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Yuejiang Liu, Azalia Mirhoseini
